verdict.rationale: Cal.com documents a self-hostable, 100% MIT-licensed edition (Cal.diy) that runs from source with no license key. That edition is a fork with all enterprise and commercial code removed, so it lacks Teams, Organizations, Workflows, Insights and SSO/SAML, and is not the full scheduling engine. Users also report that public Docker images are being discontinued, so you must build containers yourself, and that Cal.diy docs position it as personal, non-production use. missing for 10: open-source self-hosting of the full engine including team/org/workflow features, official prebuilt container images, a production-supported open-source deployment path.
